title: A domain whose localizations at maximal ideals are normal domains is a normal domain
statement: Let $R$ be an integral domain such that for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset R$ the localization $R_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $R$ is a normal domain (integrally closed in its field of fractions). In particular an integral domain which is a normal ring is a normal domain.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030B (lemma-normality-is-local, algebra.tex line 8177), implication (3) => (1) and its proof

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: `theorem IsIntegrallyClosed.of_localization_maximal [IsDomain R] (h : ∀ p : Ideal R, p ≠ ⊥ → [p.IsMaximal] → IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)) : IsIntegrallyClosed R` (IntegrallyClosed.lean:69-71, read with sed -n 55,100p, 2026-10-10); a normal domain is `IsDomain ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed` by the match of def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, so the hypothesis 'R_m normal domain for every maximal m' gives h (dropping p ≠ ⊥); the 'in particular' clause restricts the normal-ring hypothesis to maximal ideals
